description.narrative: These project Purpose (global objective) is to support the alignment of the national legislation and practice in Ukraine with European standards in the areas of media freedom and human rights protection. The project's Specific objectives, implemented through three project components, are as follows: 1.To support independence of the public broadcasting, improving safety of journalists; enhancing access to public information and personal data protection; 2.To strengthen the Ombudspersons institutional capacity in the areas of prevention of human rights violations, data protection and antidiscrimination advocacy; 3.To promote human rights-compliant management of prisons as well as further development of a rehabilitative approach to offenders.

comment.narrative: 50 journalists trained on physical and digital safety of journalists in 2017 The Guide for the implementation of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe Recommendation Rec 20164 on the protection of journalism and safety of journalists and other media actors has been translated into Ukrainian and distributed among stakeholders in 2018. The process of creating a national Rapid Response Mechanism has been launched.

Minimum 5 alerts registered at the newly created Rapid Response Mechanism for protection of media actors Rapid Response Mechanism for protection of media actors introduced in by the end of 201920 and launched at public event.

The idea of creation of Rapid response mechanism for protection of media actors in the form of information resource portal explaining the rights of journalists and showing map of infringement of journalists professional rights was widely discussed with the national stakeholders and it was included to the Recommendations of the Parliamentary Hearing Safety of journalistic activity in Ukraine current situation challenges and way of their addressing held on 6 November 2019 in the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine 4.2. to create a Rapid Response Mechanism for the protection of journalists in the form of hot line information resource portal with explanations of the rights of journalists in cooperation with the Ministry of Culture Youth and Sport of Ukraine Ministry of Internal Affairs National Police the Office of the Prosecutor General State Bureau of Investigations and civil society organisations.Based on the above mentioned the draft Concept of such a Rapid response mechanism was developed with the support of the Component. However in the end of 2020 the meetings with mediarelated civil society organisations identified the need to establish a dialogue platform as a form of rapid response mechanism in Ukraine instead of webportal creation since the lack of communication with the law enforcement agencies was admitted. Therefore the Project facilitated the establishment of the dialogue platform under auspices of the Office of the Prosecutor General in Ukraine regarding crimes against journalists which launched periodic communication and regular sectoral meetings on the progress in pretrial investigations of crimes against journalists and other media actors.

comment.narrative: 50 journalists trained on physical and digital safety of journalists in 2017 The Guide for the implementation of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe Recommendation Rec 20164 on the protection of journalism and safety of journalists and other media actors has been translated into Ukrainian and distributed among stakeholders in 2018. The process of creating a national Rapid Response Mechanism has been launched.

Minimum 5 alerts registered at the newly created Rapid Response Mechanism for protection of media actors Rapid Response Mechanism for protection of media actors introduced in by the end of 201920 and launched at public event.

The idea of creation of Rapid response mechanism for protection of media actors in the form of information resource portal explaining the rights of journalists and showing map of infringement of journalists professional rights was widely discussed with the national stakeholders and it was included to the Recommendations of the Parliamentary Hearing Safety of journalistic activity in Ukraine current situation challenges and way of their addressing held on 6 November 2019 in the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine 4.2. to create a Rapid Response Mechanism for the protection of journalists in the form of hot line information resource portal with explanations of the rights of journalists in cooperation with the Ministry of Culture Youth and Sport of Ukraine Ministry of Internal Affairs National Police the Office of the Prosecutor General State Bureau of Investigations and civil society organisations.Based on the above mentioned the draft Concept of such a Rapid response mechanism was developed with the support of the Component. However in the end of 2020 the meetings with mediarelated civil society organisations identified the need to establish a dialogue platform as a form of rapid response mechanism in Ukraine instead of webportal creation since the lack of communication with the law enforcement agencies was admitted. Therefore the Project facilitated the establishment of the dialogue platform under auspices of the Office of the Prosecutor General in Ukraine regarding crimes against journalists which launched periodic communication and regular sectoral meetings on the progress in pretrial investigations of crimes against journalists and other media actors.

comment.narrative: On 31 December 2019 the final stage of the reform of state and communal print media came to an end. As of 18 December 2018 out of 760 state and communal print media that were operational 343 were reorganised. As of 15 February 2020 615 state and communal print media outlets had been transformed into an independent media. However most of these newly reformed media face number of challenges that restrain them from successful functioning.Upon privatisation the reformed print media outlets have been stripped of their funding from local budgets which left them in a difficult situation. Moreover local municipalities failed to implement a legal provision that was supposed to give the reformed media priority access to coverage of activities run by local governments. That further undermined the reformed media outlets reducing their access to information. In addition not all local authorities in Ukraine transferred the property of the former municipalityowned media to the newly formed media outlets or concluded lease agreements for a period of 15 years with them as required by law.

As of 15 February 2020 615 state and communal print media outlets had been transformed into an independent media. However most of these newly reformed media face number of challenges that restrain them from successful functioning.The financial unstable situation of the local media in Ukraine had repercussions on their audience figures. Over the last three years the circulation of local media has gone down by an average of 30 in some cases by 50. All that has affected the financial health of many local print media companies in Ukraine with large expenses for paper printing and distribution many of them are expected to decrease their frequency or even fold. comment.narrative: On 31 December 2019 the final stage of the reform of state and communal print media came to an end. As of 18 December 2018 out of 760 state and communal print media that were operational 343 were reorganised. As of 15 February 2020 615 state and communal print media outlets had been transformed into an independent media. However most of these newly reformed media face number of challenges that restrain them from successful functioning.The financial unstable situation of the local media in Ukraine had repercussions on their audience figures. Over the last three years the circulation of local media has gone down by an average of 30 in some cases by 50. All that has affected the financial health of many local print media companies in Ukraine with large expenses for paper printing and distribution many of them are expected to decrease their frequency or even fold. The State Committee for Television and Radio Broadcasting has developed a proposal for the support of local media that was supposed to be implemented in the period 20202023. The proposal mentions financial assistance by local government and state authorities legal tools such as laws preventing increases in the tariffs for delivery of print publications tax benefits for local media in the border areas and state financial support to cover printing costs. The proposal envisages the funding model of local media to also consist of commercial revenue raised through sales of advertising and subscriptions.
